note: Multiple recent reports confirm SNUPN variants can manifest as spinocerebellar atrophy/ataxia with minimal or no overt muscle disease, as well as an asymptomatic neuroimaging finding in LGMDR29.

evidence.text: Biallelic SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy characterized by cerebellar ataxia and Purkinje cell pathology, expanding the clinical phenotype beyond skeletal muscle; one patient presented without skeletal muscle changes while another showed only mild changes.

source.title: SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy by disrupting global splicing in cerebellar Purkinje cells
source.quote: We identified pathogenic variants in the SNUPN gene in two families with spinocerebellar atrophy. One patient exhibited mild changes in skeletal muscle, while the other did not.

evidence.text: In a report of siblings with SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy presenting with adult-onset myopathy, one patient demonstrated asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy on brain neuroimaging.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: One patient presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy.
